title: 12% SDS-PAGE Western Blot
author: Grace Basa
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rwrd7d6
materials: Obtain materials Western Blot Gel Pouring Apparatus: green casting stands, 4 large glass plates, 4 small glass plates, plastic Western Blot holder for the casting stands, and combs.
Grab the following materials for 12% SDS-PAGE gels: Lower buffer (Tris 0.5M-pH 8.8), upper buffer (Tris 1.5M-pH 6.8), water, 30% Acrylamide-Bis 37.5:1, 10% SDS, 10% AP, and TEMED.
Grab materials for running a gel: Western blot running container, lid with electrodes, 1X tank buffer, gels, samples, buffer dam (if running one gel), and gel holders.

Grab the following materials to make the transfer 'sandwich': transfer tank and lid, small magnetic stir bar, ice pack, transfer electrodegel cassette, 2 sponges, Whatman blot paper, Immobilon membrane, 1X transfer buffer, methanol, one plastic tub to fit membrane, and another tub to fill with transfer buffer.
After letting the primary antibodies rock overnight, pour it back into the original container. Grab your secondary antibodies and let it thaw.
After washing, pour on your secondary antibodies after it has completely thawed. Secondary antibodies are light sensitive so wrap your container with aluminum foil.
Use the LI-COR machines to analyze your membrane.
After blocking is done, dump the blocking buffer out. Pour the primary antibodies in the container and let it rock overnight in the cold room.
While your membrane is blocking, thaw your primary antibodies.

steps.title: Sanitize glass plates
steps.instruction: Spray the glass plates with 70% ethanol and let them dry.

steps.title: Gather gel casting apparatus
steps.instruction: Collect green casting stands, four large glass plates, four small glass plates, a plastic Western blot gel holder, and combs.

steps.title: Assemble casting stand
steps.instruction: Place a small glass plate on top of a large plate, slide the pair into a green casting stand ensuring the plates are even, close the stand and clip the assembly onto the plastic gel holder.

steps.title: Prepare resolving gel buffers
steps.instruction: For lower buffer (1.5 M Tris, pH 8.8) weigh 90.85 g Tris base, dissolve in 350 mL H₂O, adjust pH to 8.8 with concentrated HCl, and bring to 500 mL with H₂O; for upper buffer (0.5 M Tris, pH 6.8) weigh 30.25 g Tris base, dissolve in 350 mL H₂O, adjust pH to 6.8 with concentrated HCl, and bring to 500 mL with H₂O.

steps.title: Pour resolving gel
steps.instruction: Using a 1000 µL pipette, fill the space between the glass plates with the resolving gel solution until reaching the bottom of the green section of the casting stand; pipette isopropanol onto the gel surface to prevent evaporation; let polymerize for ~30 min, checking polymerization with leftover solution.

steps.title: Prepare stacking gel (no TEMED)
steps.instruction: While the resolving gel polymerizes, prepare the stacking gel solution using the same buffer recipes but omit TEMED until ready to pour.

steps.title: Remove isopropanol and rinse gel
steps.instruction: When the resolving gel has polymerized, discard the isopropanol into the sink and rinse the gel surface with water.

steps.title: Polymerize stacking gel
steps.instruction: Add TEMED to the stacking gel solution, pipette the mixture up to the top of the short glass plate, insert the chosen comb ensuring no bubbles, and let polymerize for ~30 min, confirming with leftover solution.

steps.title: Store polymerized gels
steps.instruction: Wrap each gel with a moist paper towel and place in a 4 °C refrigerator until use.

steps.title: Place gels in holders
steps.instruction: Insert each gel into its gel holder with the short plate and wells facing the interior; if running a single gel, add a buffer dam on the opposite side; close the holders and place them in the electrophoresis tank.

steps.title: Denature samples
steps.instruction: Add sample buffer to protein samples (if not already added) and boil for 5 minutes to denature.

steps.title: Fill tank and gel holder with buffer
steps.instruction: Fill the electrophoresis tank with 1X tank buffer up to the line appropriate for the number of gels, and fill the interior of each gel holder with tank buffer to the very top.

steps.title: Load ladder and samples
steps.instruction: Pipette 10 µL of molecular‑weight ladder into the first well, then load each denatured sample from its Eppendorf tube into the remaining wells.

steps.title: Assemble Western blot apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the lid on the apparatus, aligning electrode colors, and connect the power cables to the matching colored ports.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run the gel at 160 V for 1 hour, checking every 8–10 minutes for buffer leaks; if leakage occurs, pause the run and use a pipette to add buffer from the tank to the gel holder.

steps.title: Dislodge gel from plates
steps.instruction: After electrophoresis, remove the gel from the glass plates and cut away the stacking gel with a razor blade.

steps.title: Pre‑wet membrane with methanol
steps.instruction: Fill a small plastic tub with methanol and immerse the Immobilon membrane to activate it.

steps.title: Assemble transfer sandwich
steps.instruction: Layer in order: black side of cassette, sponge, Whatman blotting paper, gel, pre‑wet membrane, blotting paper, sponge, clear side of cassette; keep the sandwich wet with transfer buffer.

steps.title: Remove bubbles with Sharpie
steps.instruction: Roll a Sharpie marker over the assembled sandwich to eliminate any trapped bubbles.

steps.title: Insert sandwich into electrode
steps.instruction: Close the sandwich and place it into the transfer electrode so that the cassette’s black side aligns with the electrode’s black side.

steps.title: Prepare transfer tank
steps.instruction: Insert the transfer electrode into the tank, add a magnetic stir bar to the bottom, place an ice pack inside, and fill the tank with 1X transfer buffer.

steps.title: Transfer proteins
steps.instruction: Set the lid with matching colored connections, plug in the power cables, and run the transfer at 0.4 A for 2 hours while stirring the buffer at 50 rpm.

steps.title: Recycle methanol and buffer
steps.instruction: Pour any remaining methanol and transfer buffer back into their original containers for reuse.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Place the membrane in a clear plastic container, add ~5 mL blocking buffer, and rock on a rocker for 1 hour.

steps.title: Wash membrane (first)
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane three times with 1X PBS‑Tween.

steps.title: Rock membrane (second hour)
steps.instruction: Keep the container on a rocker for an additional 1 hour.

steps.title: Wash membrane (second)
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane three more times with 1X PBS‑Tween, keeping the container wrapped in foil during washes.

steps.title: Dry membrane
steps.instruction: Remove the membrane and gently dry it between two Whatman blotting papers before imaging with the LI‑COR system.
